summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic pancreatitis, asthma, lipodermatosclerosis, and recurrent cellulitis was admitted for fever, productive cough, and increased leg erythema. She was evaluated for possible infection, but imaging and labs showed no pneumonia, bacteremia, urinary tract infection, or influenza. A viral upper respiratory infection was diagnosed as the cause of her fever and respiratory symptoms. She also experienced transient headaches, which resolved with analgesics and were found to have no intracranial cause on CT. Neck swelling was noted but imaging showed no abscess or structural abnormality. Leg swelling improved with reinstitution of furosemide after missed doses. She remained afebrile throughout her stay, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home on her baseline medications with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
Swelling, mass, or lump in head and neck
Ulcer of other part of lower limb
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
